title: Define Dedicated Capacity SLA/SLOs, Error Budgets, and Canary Guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define production SLA and SLO targets for Dedicated capacity customers, establish error budget accounting and burn-rate thresholds, and formalize automated canary/rollout gates for model and runtime changes. This ticket captures product requirements, acceptance criteria, measurement plans, and rollout policies to be used by engineering and SRE during launch and ongoing operations.
background: Dedicated customers require predictable latency and availability guarantees distinct from hosted multi-tenant tiers. Past incidents (INC-2024-11-kv-cache-thundering) exposed gaps in how we surface SLO burns and when to halt a rollout. This PRD synthesizes learnings: we need clear per-customer SLO rolls, cross-customer global fallbacks, and deterministic canary guardrails to avoid cascading outages during model or runtime upgrades.
decision: Adopt a two-tier SLO model for Dedicated: Availability SLO (99.95% monthly for API success [%2xx]) and Tail Latency SLO (95th <= 120ms, 99th <= 450ms for gen endpoints under baseline load). Error budget uses monthly window; auto-hold trigger at 30% monthly burn-rate over a 6-hour rolling window. Canary gates: progressive ramping by traffic percentage with automated rollback on burn-rate exceed or error spike.
rollout_policy: Canary sequence: 0.5% for 30m, 2% for 2h, 10% for 12h, 50% for 24h, 100% after 72h. Gates evaluated at each step: API error rate (5xx) delta, customer-specific latency p95 delta, KV cache miss ratio, and cost-per-token deviation. Automatic rollback triggers: (1) >20% increase in 5xx vs baseline for the canary cohort sustained >10m; (2) burn-rate >30% of monthly budget in 6h window for cohort; (3) p95 latency regression >2x baseline for cohort. Rollouts must record a rollout_run id and link to the canary dashboard for auditability.
acceptance_criteria: SLOs documented in product spec and approved by SRE and Engineering
Grafana dashboards (canary + per-customer SLO view) created and linked
Automated canary orchestration supports configured ramp percentages and can trigger rollback on defined thresholds
Error budget accounting computed per-customer and available via Console with clear time-window selection
Alerting: burn-rate and SLO breach alerts with runbook links wired to PagerDuty
Integration tests: synthetic load harness that validates canary gates under controlled failures (increased 5xx, latency spikes)
Runbook updated with manual mitigation steps and escalation path
measurement_methodology: Use per-request telemetry: status_code, backend_latency_ms, model_variant, customer_id, and compute_region. SLOs computed from raw logs (5xx counts for availability, backend_latency_ms for latency SLOs) with a monthly rolling window. Normalize for scheduled maintenance windows using maintenance tags. Error budget burn rate calculated hourly and evaluated by cohort and global aggregates. All metrics stored in metrics.redwood-prod and surfaced in dedicated/grafana/slo dashboards.
notes: 2025-02-25: SRE prefers a more conservative p95 target (100ms) for high-tier customers; decided to keep 120ms as baseline and offer premium 99.99%/p95=100ms as an SLA add-on
2025-02-28: Legal requested explicit exclusion clause for customer-managed network outages; added to PRD
2025-03-01: Observability team proposed per-route synthetic canaries to detect model-induced regressions; accepted as part of measurement plan
progress_updates: 2025-02-21: Drafted initial SLO numbers and shared with SRE/Eng for feedback
2025-02-26: Eng team prototyped canary controller hooks and simulated rollbacks in staging (ENG-4302)
2025-03-03: Design review scheduled to validate Console UX for per-customer SLO views
review_feedback: SRE: prefer hourly burn-rate evaluation and a 6-hour rapid-burn window for auto-holds
Security: confirm that KMS latency won't skew latency SLOs for private deployments
PM: ensure customer-visible SLA text aligns with billing and crediting logic
open_questions: Should we provide a self-serve slider in Console to allow customers to opt into stricter SLO tiers?
How do we attribute traffic for multi-tenant hosters running both Dedicated and Hosted workloads on shared infra?
Do we require legal sign-off for automated rollback that may impact customer throughput during an upgrade?
final_criteria_notes: Before release the canary controller must demonstrate two successful end-to-end rollouts in staging with synthetic failure injections and must produce audit logs for each stage transition. The Console must show per-customer remaining error budget and a button to pause rollouts for that customer.
